name: referenced-include
title: Record once, include anywhere
summary: A verified badge (a small canvas with a circle and a tick) recorded once with referencedOperations and placed after three names with include; the document is 900 B against 1163 B with the badge written out three times.
prompt: A reviewers list (Margaret Hamilton, Ken Thompson, Linus Torvalds, Frances Allen) where every name but Linus's has the same small blue verified tick after it; draw the tick once and reuse it.
teaches: Record a fragment once with {"referencedOperations": {"name": "Verified", "children": [...]}}: it is stored, not shown
Place it wherever it is needed with {"include": {"value": "@Verified"}}: the player splices the recorded components in at that spot
Prefer it over copying for anything drawn more than once without parameters (icons, dividers, logos); use definePattern when the copies differ
pitfalls: Declare referencedOperations at the top level of a root array, next to definePattern: there it is recorded in the first pass. Declared inside a column it is also drawn where it is declared, and in the C++ player its includes then lose components
A recording has no parameters: every include is identical. For a label or colour that changes, use a template (STR-06, RU-05)
The included canvas keeps its own size modifiers; give the canvas a fixed size, since it has no intrinsic size

snippets.note: the recording: one 18 dp canvas with the tick

check.describe: Four names under REVIEWERS; Margaret Hamilton, Ken Thompson and Frances Allen each followed by the same blue circle with a white tick, Linus Torvalds without. Resized (narrow 240, wide 540) the list keeps its left edge and each tick follows its name; the rows are as wide as their content, so nothing depends on the header width.
